title: Latency-aware selective verification in generate–validate NetOps pipelines
research_question: Can a selective, low-latency verification tier (risk-scoring + fast validator) integrated into a generate–validate–repair pipeline for LLM-generated network changes reduce unsafe commits versus LLM-only while meeting a preregistered end-to-end latency SLO?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1 (safety): The selective low-latency verification intervention yields a lower unsafe-commit rate (proportion of proposals that are unsafe per full-checker ground truth) than LLM-only on the same intent set (paired comparison).

H2 (latency + joint claim): The selective verification intervention meets the preregistered latency SLO: 95th-percentile end-to-end pipeline latency ≤ 2000 ms; its 95th-percentile latency is statistically lower than the full-verification baseline while providing materially lower unsafe-commit rate than LLM-only.
exploratory_questions: How does the unsafe-commit reduction vary with the selective-verifier threshold (budget trade-off curve)?
How do adversarial / out-of-distribution (OOD) intents affect selective-verifier false-negative rates relative to in-distribution intents?
What is the verification budget (fraction verified) at which marginal safety gains diminish (Pareto frontier)?
benchmark_scope: Synthetic operator-intent corpus (publicly shareable generator) representing common change tasks: ACL changes, route addition/removal (static/BGP/OSPF), and interface configuration edits.
Two vendor-family semantic models (VendorFamily-A, VendorFamily-B) at configuration/semantics abstraction level supported by the experiment Docker image digital-twin.
secondary_estimands: Absolute 95th-percentile end-to-end latency per intervention (with bootstrap CIs)
Verification budget (fraction of proposals sent to fast verifier) vs unsafe-commit rate curve
False-negative rate among adversarial / OOD intents
sampling_plan: Confirmatory paired design. Confirmatory item count = 400 unique operator intents (same intent presented to each condition: baseline=LLM-only; guarded=selective low-latency verifier). Fixed random seed for intent ordering. Per-intent: one generation per condition. Planned_model_calls = 400 tasks * 2 conditions * 1 generation = 800 LLM generations. The confirmatory corpus deterministically includes 10% adversarial/OOD variants (40 intents) per preregistered perturbation rules. A separate synthetic discovery/training set of 2000 labeled intent→config pairs (discovery_items=2000) is generated and labeled via the full-checker for risk-classifier training and threshold calibration; discovery items are not part of confirmatory analysis.
power_and_precision_plan: Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Target effect: absolute reduction in unsafe-commit rate of 5 percentage points (e.g., from 8% to 3%) between baseline (LLM-only) and guarded (selective verifier). Clustering unit: intent (paired). Calculation method: exact paired-proportion power approximation and preregistered simulation script (frozen). For N=400 paired items, under planning assumptions (baseline unsafe ≈8%, selective ≈3%), estimated power > 0.8 for two-sided alpha=0.05. Sensitivity analyses: recompute power for baseline rates 5% and 12%; simulate varying within-pair correlation; rerun primary analysis treating infrastructure-failure pairs as unsafe (conservative).
exclusion_rules: Exclude pairs from primary analysis if any condition for that intent suffers unrecovered infrastructure failure (per missingness_plan: 'complete_pair_primary').
Deterministic parsing failures of LLM output after allowed retries are recorded as generation failures and trigger exclusion per above rule.
No ad-hoc exclusions; any additional exclusions must be logged and justified in revision log.
missingness_plan: Define infrastructure failures a priori. LLM/provider transient failures: retry policy up to 2 additional attempts with exponential backoff (500 ms, then 1500 ms). If generation still unavailable, mark as infrastructure failure. Primary analysis excludes incomplete pairs ('complete_pair_primary'). Sensitivity analysis treats infrastructure-failure pairs as unsafe ('complete_pair_primary_with_failure_as_zero_sensitivity') to obtain conservative bounds. All retries, timestamps, and failure artifacts logged and hashed in the execution manifest.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: use available analysis executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 to compute the primary estimand paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline on complete pairs only. Compute per-condition unsafe-commit rates with exact 95% binomial CIs. Apply McNemar-equivalent paired logic implemented by paired_binary_analysis_v1 for hypothesis testing (H1). Latency analysis: compute per-intent end-to-end latencies for guarded and baseline pipelines; compute 95th-percentiles with bootstrap CIs; compare 95th-percentiles using paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests for selective vs full-checker latency and selective vs baseline where appropriate. For H2 latency comparison against full-verification baseline: measure full-checker (digital-twin) check time per intent deterministically (applied to the same generated configuration) and compare to selective pipeline latencies. Multiplicity: primary confirmatory family limited to H1 and H2; report unadjusted p-values for primary tests and FDR-adjusted values for exploratory scans. Predefine subgroup analyses (adversarial vs non-adversarial) and threshold sweeps; label exploratory.
multiplicity_plan: Two preregistered confirmatory hypotheses (H1, H2). All other tests (threshold sweeps, subgroups) are exploratory. When reporting multiple exploratory comparisons, control FDR via Benjamini–Hochberg at q=0.05 and present both unadjusted and adjusted p-values.

If infrastructure disruption prevents completion within capability manifest constraints, abort and report with full execution manifest.
